headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict pathways; RD-Agent’s Docker isolation does not protect Goose’s default host access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, while RD-Agent can run browsers and broad network egress. A shared filesystem bridge makes attacker-controlled files or outputs plausible instruction carriers. The interaction is inferred from both profiles; no direct sandbox evidence blocks it.
conditions: IF Goose reads files produced by RD-Agent without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF RD-Agent writes browser-derived content into shared files, Goose may parse it as instructions.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic parsing of shared files.
Require provenance tags on inter-agent artifacts.
Review MCP tool outputs before reuse.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd and has broad egress; RD-Agent handles logs, execution traces, and financial/research data and calls external APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive material can flow from one agent into the other and then out via network calls. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary between them.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same cwd or log directory, leakage risk increases.
IF Goose forwards shared files to configured model providers, sensitive data can exit the environment.
IF RD-Agent stores traces containing secrets in shared files, Goose can read them.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Redact logs and traces before sharing.
Disable file upload from shared workspaces.
Rotate any exposed API keys.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem. RD-Agent also supports multiple instances and writes logs. Concurrent access to the same repo or cwd can corrupt files or git state; no locking is documented. This is a direct pairwise conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or cwd, file races can occur.
IF Goose commits while RD-Agent edits the same tree, git state can diverge.
IF either agent lacks external locking, concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories.
Serialize git operations.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
Run one agent at a time for mutable repos.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code or shell actions, and RD-Agent is an automation/research agent that may consume outputs as inputs. If RD-Agent treats Goose-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream analysis or actions. The profiles do not document verification gates, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF RD-Agent ingests Goose outputs without validation, mistakes propagate.
IF Goose emits malformed code or commands that RD-Agent reuses, downstream failures can cascade.
IF either agent auto-executes the other's artifacts, impact increases.
mitigations: Add explicit verification steps.
Require human review for generated artifacts.
Compare outputs against tests or schemas.
Quarantine untrusted inter-agent files.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware workflow gating.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and multiple third-party APIs, while Goose handles source code and local files with broad egress. If regulated or confidential data is placed in the shared workflow, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches. Goose is open-source and local, but RD-Agent’s external API use makes compliance boundaries relevant.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through RD-Agent APIs, residency or retention obligations may be triggered.
IF Goose reads the same files, local handling may violate least-privilege expectations.
IF logs or traces contain personal or financial data, retention mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Review API/data-processing terms.
Minimize logs and traces.
Delete temporary artifacts promptly.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing and retention controls.
